PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT / V0.0 / DEVELOPMENT BASELINE

SaveSphere

A single-owner, self-hosted personal operating system for managing life, preserving knowledge and making informed decisions.

Product type Single-owner self-hosted software Platforms Angular web / PWA on Windows & Linux · Android phone & tablet Audience One owner / developer / operator
Product thesis

SaveSphere brings personal domains and saved knowledge into one owner-controlled system. Today supports daily action; Life modules own canonical records; Knowledge preserves originals and supports authoring; Insights and Assistant use permitted evidence. The self-hosted canonical platform supports authenticated web access and native Android capture, S Pen notes and supported offline workflows.

00 / Document guide

The founding development specification for SaveSphere.

Document contract

SaveSphere is a greenfield, single-owner personal operating system developed independently from scratch. Its requirements define intended product capabilities rather than compatibility with, migration from, or replacement of any predecessor application. External data import, interoperability, portability, backup and restoration are first-class capabilities where explicitly specified.

The repository is a specification-stage project. Application build, deployment and runtime verification are not established by this document. The owner is the product decision-maker, developer and operator; implementation evidence is recorded separately from the requirements.

How to read this specification

Read product and platform boundaries first, then the owning module and its detailed contracts. Consult the shared privacy, data, offline and quality rules before implementing a change. The roadmap assigns delivery increments; the register links each requirement to its phase, prerequisites, applicability and acceptance evidence.

Canonical requirement source

This HTML file is the authoritative product specification, including its narrative, requirement definitions, acceptance criteria, register, delivery metadata, entities and roadmap work packages. Edit it directly. Its content and styles are stored in this file; no generation step is required. Embedded structured data supports local filters and exports and must remain consistent with the visible definitions. See the documentation workflow for the build and validation commands.

Module and requirement counts describe this baseline and may grow through approved product decisions. GOV-01 defines scope governance. Requirement identifiers freeze when implementation starts; the Knowledge sequence is consecutive in this founding baseline.

Requirement fields

FieldPurpose
Requirement IDStable implementation and test reference.
Owner / moduleAuthoritative business or platform responsibility.
PriorityImportance to the product; not a delivery date.
Target phasePlanned delivery increment.
DependenciesPrerequisite requirements; links also expose dependents.

Scope statusRequired, conditional, deferred or explicitly optional.

Priority describes importance: P0 is essential foundation/core utility, P1 is important domain depth, and P2 is advanced capability. Target phase is the delivery plan. Dependencies identify prerequisite contracts or explicitly bounded prototype increments. Feasibility records the conditions to verify. These are separate fields; an early feasibility prototype does not mean the complete feature is delivered.

Implementation status starts as Not verified : this document has no implementation evidence. Acceptance evidence starts as Not recorded . Requirements whose priorities are marked proposed require an explicit owner decision before that priority is frozen.

Scope and delivery states

StateMeaning
RequiredRequired at the assigned scope.
ConditionalRequired when the stated feasibility condition is satisfied.
DeferredRequired in a later planned increment.
OptionalOwner-selected extension; not required for base acceptance.
Out Of ScopeExcluded by an approved scope decision.

Blocked is a delivery status caused by an unresolved prerequisite; it does not change the underlying scope. In a mixed requirement, an explicitly optional or provider-conditional extension keeps that qualifier while the specified manual behavior and fallback remain required.

01 / Product definition

A private personal operating system, not a collection of disconnected trackers.

Problem statement

Personal information is scattered across calendars, notes, financial records, health apps, documents, possessions and projects. SaveSphere connects those records into a single system that the owner controls, without needing to operate a public SaaS or rely on a separate consumer subscription.

Product vision

Give the owner one durable, private system for managing daily life, preserving information and making evidence-based decisions. SaveSphere connects finances, productivity, health, goals, habits, faith, relationships, career, possessions, lifestyle and projects with rich notes, original documents, search and automation. Structured domain records and unstructured evidence share identity, permissions, provenance and links while keeping their authoritative roles distinct.

The owner operates a home-hosted canonical server, uses the complete web workspace from approved browsers, and uses supported Android workflows online or offline. The host may also be an interactive workstation; deployment must isolate production resources and development. Device and task context select the best entry point. Manual core workflows remain useful without model inference.

Product hierarchy

SaveSphere has eight navigation destinations, logical business modules and shared platform services. Navigation groups are conveniences, not competing product taxonomies or service boundaries.

LayerRole

InboxCapture and review.

KnowledgeAuthoring and preservation; Library is a view.
LifePersonal domain management.
InsightsAnalytics and dashboards.
AssistantPersonal intelligence under one shared policy.

Functional modulesCanonical domain ownership and business logic; current module count is recorded in this document.
Shared platform servicesIdentity, storage, sync, privacy, search, AI orchestration, events, audit, analytics and notifications.

Product principles

Principle Implication
Single owner No public signup, multi-tenancy, subscription tiers, advertising or shared household workspaces.
One system, many modules Shared records, search, calendar, attachments and links; independently enabled modules.
Offline-first Android Local durable writes and visible reconciliation; PostgreSQL remains canonical.
Data ownership Self-hosted storage, export, encrypted backups and explicit connector consent.
Human in control AI proposals are distinct from facts and approved actions; no unauthorized external writes.
Useful without AI Core capture, planning, finance, search and dashboards do not require inference.
Progressive depth Fast capture and Today view; advanced management and analytics available on demand.
Evidence over assumptions Show data provenance, freshness, completeness and uncertainty; no invented or silently duplicated records.

Non-goals

Public SaaS, public registration, household sharing, app marketplace, multi-tenant scaling, commercial onboarding, billing, and customer support are outside scope. Native iOS and HealthKit are future P2 conditional expansion, not part of the initial Android/web release. SaveSphere is not a bank, broker, medical device, diagnostic or emergency service, surveillance platform, or substitute for licensed professional advice. It does not promise financial outcomes or autonomously perform high-risk actions.

First-class knowledge and preservation capabilities

SaveSphere replaces the need to remember the original app, device or folder. A saved item is retrievable by title, content, meaning, source, visual clues, relationships or time. It is simultaneously a notes authoring workspace, a digital archive, a personal search engine and the knowledge layer for all functional domains. Original artifacts, editable content and AI-derived interpretations remain distinct.

Knowledge capability Required outcome
Universal capture Share, write, dictate, scan, import, watch or connect; capture first and classify later.
Personal notes Everyday typed, handwritten, mixed-media, PDF and visual notes, with offline Android and complete web access.
Personal memory Evidence-grounded search, answers, related knowledge, summaries and proactive rediscovery.
Preservation Original bytes, source provenance, revisions, verification, export and recoverability without a proprietary service.

Destination / capability Required outcome

Life Maintain complete domain workflows across all functional modules, independently enabled and useful without needing notes or AI.
Insights Measure, visualize, compare, forecast and review structured life records with transparent calculations, assumptions and freshness.
Inbox Save anything supported from anywhere; preserve first and classify later, including offline Android capture.

Knowledge is an independent workspace and a shared evidence foundation. Domain modules own their validated facts. Product balance follows usefulness and dependencies, without a fixed allocation of feature counts or development hours.

The central loop is capture, interpret, organize, schedule, act, reflect and improve. A capture can produce several typed proposals, but each confirmed transaction, task or document has one canonical identity regardless of how many views display it. No module requires AI for its core manual workflows. Adaptive planning and nonjudgmental recovery are ordinary product behavior.

02 / Owner & platforms

One owner, developer and operator; platform roles define capabilities and access boundaries.

Owner profile and operating assumptions

The owner develops and operates the product, uses a home desktop that normally remains powered on, and wants a deep engineering project that becomes useful in everyday life. The home desktop hosts production services while remaining a normal interactive workstation. There is no second owner, public enrollment or commercial deployment. Device identity and purpose-based scopes still matter even when all clients belong to one person.

Platform roles and access boundaries

Device Primary surface Primary workflows / boundaries
Home desktop Angular (local or HTTPS); server host Complete command center, bulk editing, imports, dashboards, configuration, development and operations. Keep production and development isolated.
Personal Linux laptop Angular browser / optional PWA Complete remote management over HTTPS; no VPN client. Online-first.
supported Android phone Expo Android app Offline capture and editing, workouts, habits, expenses, scans, notifications, journal, notes, Health Connect.
supported Android stylus tablet Tablet-adaptive Expo; optional Angular browser Split-pane planner, reading, journaling, dashboards, First-class S Pen handwriting, PDF markup, hybrid notes and offline editing.
Work laptop Angular restricted Work Mode Selected personal tasks, reminders, career/learning and approved notes, subject to employer policy; no sensitive caches.
Work desktop Angular restricted Work Mode Same restricted scope; no access to server administration or sensitive life domains.
Work-device caveat: employer-managed computers may be monitored. Server-enforced scope is not a guarantee of privacy; never import employer-confidential records, credentials or source code without authorization. Use personal devices for sensitive information.

Primary jobs

  • Plan the day, prioritize tasks and track progress against personal goals.
  • Capture information instantly, even without a network; organize and link it later.
  • Understand spending, health, learning, projects and possessions using trusted historical data.
  • Review trends, compare choices, and automate repetitive activities with explicit controls.
  • Operate, extend, troubleshoot and recover the system without relying on a third-party SaaS.

Initial configuration

Bootstrap the owner locally. Configure timezone, base currency, units, language, enabled modules, recovery credentials, device enrollment, notifications and backup targets. The initial values are in the owner deployment profile; preferences remain editable.

Personal computing surfaces

Windows personal computers and the Linux laptop use the full Angular web app at the owner domain; an installable PWA is the initial desktop packaging. A narrowly scoped Windows/Linux capture and watched-folder companion is a separate optional native utility, not a second full desktop client. Employer-managed Windows devices retain restricted Work Mode and must not install agents or import confidential content without authorization.

Default experience by platform role

Approved device Default landing / emphasis Preserved capabilities and limits

Personal Linux laptop Today by default; balanced management and Knowledge workspace Complete authorized Angular workspace, with direct access to research, writing, planning and analytics. Online-first.
supported Android phone Today / capture and action first Quick-add, share, notes, expenses, workouts, habits, reminders and supported offline domain operations.
supported Android stylus tablet Knowledge & Plan first; default Knowledge workspace with direct Plan and Today access First-class S Pen, PDF, rich/hybrid notes, canvas, reading, planning, dashboards and supported offline domain workflows.

The personal owner may select an authorized landing destination and dashboard layout per enrolled device. Defaults never remove features or expand permissions. An unavailable destination falls back to an authorized Today or restricted shell. Deep links, Android share intents and explicit editor launches open their requested authorized workflow directly rather than forcing a dashboard detour. Work-mode defaults and preferences cannot bypass server policy.

03 / Product experience

A bold, animated, dark-first command center with adaptive phone and tablet experiences.

Information architecture

Destination Purpose
Today Agenda, focus, habits, relevant alerts, selected signals and quick capture.
Inbox Unprocessed notes, documents, receipts, ideas, tasks and integration exceptions.
Plan Calendar, tasks, goals, routines, habits, projects, focus and time blocks.
Knowledge All saved items, notebooks, collections, smart views, rich and ink notes, PDF reader, canvases, search, source history and rediscovery.
Life Related domain groups containing the defined modules (see section 04).
Insights Custom dashboards, comparisons, trends, drill-downs and review workspaces.
Assistant Knowledge Copilot, context-aware chat, evidence, proposed actions and approvals; broader action agents later.
Settings Device enrollment, access scopes, sync, storage, backups, integrations, logs and preferences.

Today is the daily command center and default full-personal desktop landing route; Insights is the deeper analytics and dashboard-building destination. Knowledge remains a peer top-level destination with its own complete authoring environment. Assistant is the shared intelligence surface: P1 knowledge retrieval and scoped suggestions first, broader cross-domain planning, briefings, action proposals and specialist agents at their assigned priorities. Life organizes the functional modules into related navigation groups. The owner can move directly between a widget, domain record, linked evidence and the relevant editor without unnecessary navigation.

Platform responsibilities

Surface Responsibilities
Angular command center Dense responsive desktop workspace, advanced charts and grids, import/reconciliation, drag-and-drop dashboards, bulk operations, search, planning, data management, automation configuration and admin.
Expo Android companion Fast capture, manual records, offline reading/editing, native camera, share intent, biometrics, notifications, workout sessions and health/device APIs; compact phone and split-pane tablet layouts.
.NET backend Canonical records, business validation, auth, sync, jobs, integration adapters, analytics, files, AI gateway, rule engine and system operations. No direct client database access.

Core interaction model

  • Universal quick capture: text, dictation, scan, share, upload; classify and link with review.
  • Global command palette, full-text search and filters by domain, date, state and sensitivity.
  • Universal record view: details, attachments, relationships, provenance, history, activity and actions.
  • Dashboard widgets: drag, resize, filter, drill down, save per device/layout; persist layouts server-side.
  • Daily closeout, weekly and monthly reviews; missing or stale information clearly indicated.
  • Phone: bottom navigation, quick-add button, one-handed forms. Tablet: persistent navigation, split panes, landscape, keyboard and stylus where supported. Desktop: keyboard shortcuts, dense grids, resizable panels and multi-widget layouts.

Visual identity

Dark-first, with bold domain-specific accent colors, strong data hierarchy, restrained glow effects, animated counters, chart transitions, expandable panels, heatmaps and micro-interactions. Favor readable numbers, consistent spacing and meaningful motion over decoration. Support reduced motion, keyboard navigation, contrast and screen readers.

Platform behavior

Angular is online-first, optionally installable as a PWA with app-shell caching on trusted personal devices only; Windows and Linux receive the complete browser workspace. It must clearly report server unavailability; offline web editing is not an initial commitment. Android is local-first for supported records, uses encrypted persistence, and never treats an unconfirmed server operation as complete. Both clients share stable identifiers, contracts and design tokens, not UI implementations.

Knowledge workspace interaction model

  • Desktop: three-pane library / results / editor with collapsible outline, backlinks and source inspector; keyboard commands, tabbed documents, bulk selection, drag/drop and paste.
  • Tablet: full-screen ink or split-pane reading and note taking; landscape, S Pen, touch and keyboard; palm rejection and stylus-only mode. Phone: one-tap share, quick note, camera, voice and recent items.
  • Universal capture opens instantly, accepts unclassified items, and never blocks saving on OCR, AI or the network. Show durable local receipt, upload, indexing, error and review states separately.
  • Search is global and knowledge-specific; support quick filters, saved queries, pinned items, recent items, original source, snippets and evidence navigation.
  • Manual folders/notebooks, multi-membership collections, tags, favorites and dynamic smart views coexist with AI suggestions. A single item can appear in many views without duplicate binaries.

Phone navigation uses Today, Inbox, Capture, Plan and More; Capture is a central action and Calendar is a view within Plan. All desktop destinations remain accessible. More provides Life, Knowledge, Insights, Assistant and Settings; tablet uses a navigation rail and split panes. Private Review requires a fresh sensitive unlock before protected content loads. Each screen must have meaningful populated, empty, loading, error, denied, locked, offline, stale, disabled-module and retry states where relevant. Test dark and light appearance at 360 × 800 and 412 × 915 logical phone sizes, tablet landscape/portrait and desktop. Keep purple SaveSphere primary identity; use distinct domain accents, Arabic font fallback, right-to-left layout within Arabic content, accessibility labels, reduced motion, keyboard and high-contrast equivalents. Use plain text for privacy and status as well as color. No guilt-based copy or numeric faith/life scores.

04 / Functional requirements

Requirements are grouped by domain. Every module uses shared search, links, permissions, export and lifecycle behavior unless explicitly excluded.

Priority and delivery. P0, P1 and P2 describe product importance. Target phase, prerequisites, platform applicability and feasibility are separate register fields. A later target or unresolved provider condition does not remove the specified feature.

Domain group Module identifiers Representative analytics
Productivity & planning M03, M04, M20 Completion heatmaps, time allocation, goals, capacity and recovery.

M01 is the shared application shell and foundation; its placement in the intelligence group does not postpone it. All modules share common services.

System status & data health

M01-R19P1 · proposed priorityData Health
Phase 06 · M01 · Web, Android, Server · Required · Not Verified

Objective: Identify duplicate, incomplete, stale, unlinked and corrupted records across authorized domains, grouped by domain and severity.

Functional contract

Examples: likely duplicate contacts, expenses or documents; required fields missing; assets or documents without receipts or renewals; goals and projects with no activity; attachments whose hash no longer matches, orphaned blobs, broken links, failed extraction or import, unresolved sync conflicts and expired reference data. Every finding states why it was raised and links to the affected record. The dashboard proposes fixes, such as merge, link, complete, archive, restore from version or re-verify, with a preview and undo. It never repairs, merges or deletes automatically, and the owner may dismiss or snooze a finding class. Detection runs on the server within bounded resources and reports its last run and coverage. Findings and telemetry contain identifiers, not raw private content.

Acceptance criteria (1)
  1. M01-R19-AC01 Seeded duplicates, an attachment with a changed hash and an unlinked receipt each appear as findings with explanations. Accepting a merge is undoable, and a dismissed finding does not return unless the underlying data changes. A restricted domain’s findings are not visible, and not counted, in a limited session.Evidence: not recorded

Prerequisites: KN-02, ARC-03

Feasibility: Implementation and acceptance verification required; no external-provider dependency for the core manual behavior.

Applicable shared contracts: authorization, lifecycle, accessibility, offline, privacy, audit, deterministic core

M16-R13P2 · proposed priorityHistorical views
Phase 08 · M16 · Web, Android, Server · Deferred · Not Verified

Objective: Let the owner inspect historical snapshots of life metrics and plans, such as budget versus actual, net worth, goals, habits, workout volume, capacity and daily state, and see them as they were at a chosen past date.

Functional contract

Views are read-only, clearly labeled with the “as of” date, and compare any past date with the present. Use stored, versioned snapshots and record history, not values reconstructed with today’s rules, and label any metric that cannot be reconstructed rather than estimating it silently. Snapshot cadence and retention are owner-configurable, and snapshots inherit the privacy and retention rules of their source domains. Removing a record under a deletion request also removes it from affected snapshots, and a snapshot never resurrects deleted data.

M16-R11P1 · proposed priorityDecision Journal
Phase 07 · M16 · Web, Android, Server · Required · Not Verified

Objective: Let the owner record a significant decision at the time it is made: the question, options considered, chosen option, reasoning, assumptions, expected outcome and review date, linked to the records it concerns.

Functional contract

At review time, record actual outcomes and compare them with the assumptions and expectations, noting which assumptions held, failed or were untestable. Build on M16 decision records. Entries are immutable once recorded: later reflection is added as a dated amendment so the owner’s original reasoning is preserved. Surface due reviews through the normal reminder and notification rules. Comparisons are descriptive; no “decision quality score” or judgment of the owner, and no AI verdict presented as fact. Optional AI assistance is labeled and cites its evidence.

Acceptance criteria (1)
  1. M16-R11-AC01 A past decision can be reopened to show its original assumptions beside current linked data. A reflection added later does not overwrite the original text. A decision linked to a never-auto-act or private domain inherits that privacy in every view and export.Evidence: not recorded

Prerequisites: M16-R04

Feasibility: Implementation and acceptance verification required; no external-provider dependency for the core manual behavior.

Applicable shared contracts: authorization, lifecycle, accessibility, offline, privacy, audit, deterministic core

M16-R12P2 · proposed prioritySandbox simulation mode
Phase 08 · M16 · Web, Android, Server · Deferred · Not Verified

Objective: Let the owner model hypothetical schedules, budgets, goals and life changes, such as a new job, a move, a purchase or a changed routine, in a named scenario that is isolated from real records.

Functional contract

A scenario is a copy-on-write overlay on a chosen baseline snapshot. While in a scenario the interface shows a persistent, plain-text “Sandbox — not real” indicator. Nothing in a scenario may write to canonical records, sync as real data, send notifications, trigger rules or automations, call connectors, execute AI action proposals, create reminders or appear in search, insights, exports or backups as fact. The owner may compare scenarios with the baseline and with each other, state assumptions explicitly, and either discard a scenario or promote selected changes. Promotion is an explicit action that shows a diff and goes through normal validation and approval, like any other change. Simulations reuse the deterministic calculation engines and label results as projections with their assumptions.

Acceptance criteria (1)
  1. M16-R12-AC01 After building and discarding a budget and schedule scenario, no real record, notification, rule execution or sync operation has changed. A promoted change appears in the audit log as an ordinary owner action. A scenario never reads data the session is not authorized for.Evidence: not recorded

Prerequisites: M16-R04, M03-R06, M05-R03

Feasibility: Implementation and acceptance verification required; no external-provider dependency for the core manual behavior.

Applicable shared contracts: authorization, lifecycle, accessibility, offline, privacy, audit, deterministic core

05 / Knowledge specification

M09 owns Knowledge. These detailed requirements define capture, preservation, authoring, organization and retrieval; M01 supplies capture entry points, M02 supplies shared intelligence and M16 supplies rules and analytics. Individual register fields specify priority, target phase and dependencies.

B. Data import and connector strategy

Each source gets a capability matrix, import preview, mapping rules, resumable batch, error report, imported/skipped/duplicate counts and reversible batch association. Retain the export package as evidence when appropriate. Do not delete originals from source apps. The following are proposed ingestion paths; validate actual export fidelity, API access, licensing, permissions and versions before implementation.

Source Initial migration / ongoing capture Limits and fallback
Samsung Notes Owner exports available formats (PDF, image, text or native artifact where offered); import with original filename and notebooks where recoverable. Share new notes/documents. Native proprietary ink, page structure and editability may not be recoverable; preserve export and original artifact; no guaranteed live sync.
Evernote ENEX import candidate: notes, rich content, tags, attachments, created/modified times and links where present. Notebook hierarchy and unsupported markup may require mapping or manual repair; validate representative export.
OneNote Owner-exported pages/notebooks, PDF, HTML or supported Microsoft API with delegated consent where feasible. Native layouts, ink and embedded objects may lose editability; preserve original exports and report conversion losses.
WhatsApp Owner-exported chat text and optional media; parse timestamps, senders, chat context and attachment matches; share selected messages/files. No promise of continuous personal-chat API sync or decryption of private backups; preserve third-party privacy.
Teams Authorized exports, permitted Microsoft Graph integration or manual selection/share. Tenant policy, admin consent, retention and employer confidentiality govern access; do not bypass organizational restrictions.
Instagram / TikTok Share links, captions or owner-provided files; import owner account archives where available; resolve permitted metadata. Saved-list and media APIs may be restricted; no guaranteed automated download, private content or full library sync; link-only fallback.
Email EML/MBOX or permitted mailbox export; later scoped read-only OAuth/IMAP adapter, sender/thread metadata and attachments. No sending by default; explicit folders/labels, allowlists and sensitivity review; handle duplicate threads and revoked access.
Local / cloud files Bulk folder upload preserving relative paths; Windows/Linux watcher; later scoped cloud-drive connectors. No automatic deletion or bidirectional sync by default; exclude secrets, system folders and employer files; detect renamed and revised files.
Web / other apps Android share target, desktop clipboard, browser capture, manual upload, link or export import. Respect access restrictions, DRM and provider terms; never represent a link as an archived copy.
Notion Owner-provided Markdown, HTML, CSV and attachment exports, using a validated versioned adapter with import preview. Verify actual export structure, relations, databases, media and permissions; preserve original packages and report unsupported fields.
Obsidian Owner-selected Markdown vault and attachments; map folders, links, tags and supported frontmatter through a reviewed adapter. Preserve original files, detect duplicate/source IDs and explicitly report unsupported plugins, embeds or proprietary metadata.

KN-18

E. Knowledge release acceptance scenarios

  • Import a mixed external export twice; preserve originals, report skipped/unsupported items, keep tags and timestamps when available and avoid duplicate accepted items.
  • Share a video link from the phone offline; reopen after force-close; sync once and show link-only versus downloaded content accurately.
  • Write a mixed ink/text note on the supported Android stylus tablet in airplane mode, restart, reconnect, view on Windows and edit text in Linux web without losing ink.
  • Annotate a PDF, open a citation on the correct page, export an annotated copy, and verify original hash unchanged.
  • Ask a question about information distributed across a handwritten note, chat export and PDF; answer cites permitted evidence or explicitly reports missing information.
  • Manually override a suggested tag, run reclassification and verify the lock persists; disable AI for a notebook and confirm no search snippets or copilot citations leak through restricted scope.
  • Rename a watched file, interrupt its upload and retry; no duplicate artifact or accidental source deletion. Restore a backup and verify content hashes and relationships.

Knowledge in SaveSphere

Knowledge is a complete notes application and digital archive. Its storage, provenance, extraction, retrieval and Copilot contracts serve authorized life modules; rich editing, Library, notebooks, PDF and canvas remain directly accessible. Linked evidence does not replace domain validation, ledger facts, metrics, lifecycle rules or action approval.

06 / Connected workflows

The value of SaveSphere comes from connections between modules, not merely from the number of features.

Workflow Expected behavior Boundary / exception
Morning planning Today combines calendar, priority tasks, routines and relevant deadlines; optional assistant proposes a realistic plan once AI is implemented. Conflicting events and missing context are visible; owner confirms schedule changes.
Purchase to ownership Capture receipt → verify details → link transaction → create inventory item → schedule warranty/return reminders. Owner chooses whether the purchase represents a tracked asset; never double-count spending.
Monthly money review Reconcile transactions → compare budget → review recurring charges → update savings or retirement scenario. Uncategorized and stale data are flagged; no funds move automatically.
Weekly wellness review Combine permitted activity, sleep, mood, routines and goals; show descriptive trends and optional reflections. Missing records stay missing; correlations are not medical or causal claims.
Career progression Set target role → map skills → create learning plan → schedule sessions → attach evidence → review progress. No fabricated credentials or unapproved external submissions.
Home improvement Create project → add budget and material list → link receipts and manuals → schedule maintenance. Smart-device actions require the separate authorized gateway and applicable safety checks.
Outfit and event Create event → select occasion and owned garments → optionally check weather → save outfit and packing tasks. Location/weather access is optional; unavailable garments are excluded.
Side-income project Capture idea → define deliverables → track costs and revenue → generate draft invoice → review profitability. Invoices are not sent without authorization; personal and business totals reconcile.
Personal decision Describe decision → define options and weights → record assumptions → compare scenarios → set review date. The system explains scoring and uncertainty; the owner owns the decision.

Cross-module integrity rules

  • Link a shared record rather than silently copying it. A transaction can relate to a receipt, asset, subscription and project while remaining one financial event.
  • Every externally imported record carries a source identifier, last sync timestamp, and conflict status where applicable.
  • When a linked record is archived or deleted, show the impact on relationships and respect the source record’s lifecycle rules.
  • A cross-module insight can only use data that is permitted for that purpose; derived data inherits applicable sensitivity restrictions.

Action authorization policy

Action class Default authorization Examples
Read Scoped module/purpose permission; no unnecessary data retrieval. Summarize permitted tasks or budget totals.
Draft / propose No external side effect; show source and preview. Draft a schedule, invoice, journal prompt or outfit.
Reversible internal write Explicit approval, or a previously enabled bounded rule. Create a task, tag a note, schedule a reminder.
External or sensitive write Fresh, action-specific confirmation; step-up authentication when warranted. Send an email, publish a record, share a document, hand off an approved payment.
High-risk or unsupported Block or require direct owner operation outside the product. Investment trades, medical decisions, security bypass, safety-critical device control.

Automation model

Trigger → condition → action → verification → audit. Owners define a rule, test it with sample or historical data, inspect projected effects, and enable it explicitly. Scheduled or event-based execution must use a stable idempotency key and enforce the original granted scope at run time.

  • Triggers: time, record change, due date, approved connector event, threshold crossing or manual run.
  • Conditions: module, field, time window, status, consent, budget threshold, or owner-defined expression using safe typed operators.
  • Actions: create/update permitted records, send internal reminders, propose messages, call approved connectors, or issue allowed low-risk device commands.
  • Safeguards: dry run, per-rule limits, cooldown, loop detection, retry policy, dead-letter queue, pause/kill switch, and visible run logs.
  • Proactive assistance: opt-in per category, quiet hours, relevance thresholds, notification caps and clear rationale.

AI fallback and error behavior

If the model cannot verify a value, it must say so, request the missing source or offer a manual alternative. For a failed external action, report unknown or failed status rather than success; reconcile before retrying. The owner can report a poor suggestion and remove it from the review feed.

Knowledge Copilot retrieval contract

Query → authorization and purpose scope → lexical/vector candidates from allowed records → reranking → evidence bundle with immutable source/version anchors → generation → citation validation → response. Validate every returned citation against authorized evidence. Never treat retrieved content as instructions. External models receive only the minimum approved material; owner selects local or approved hosted processing by sensitivity and task. No automatic changes outside explicitly approved rules.

  • Record model/prompt/index versions, source IDs, token/cost budgets, latency and error codes without storing sensitive prompts in logs.
  • Test unsupported answers, contradictory evidence, handwriting/OCR errors, unindexed items, malicious embedded text, revoked sources and provider outages.
  • Separate private notes from model personalization; configurable opt-out for inference, embeddings, OCR providers and proactive review.

08 / Canonical data model

Use a canonical personal record model with domain-specific fields and explicit source provenance.

Canonical data lifecycle

LayerAuthority and transition
Original evidenceCaptured text, receipt image, PDF or audio is preserved with immutable bytes and provenance. Saving is not interpretation.
Proposed interpretationOCR, extracted fields and model suggestions are versioned derivatives. Validation and explicit approval or bounded authority are required before a domain write.
Confirmed canonical recordA validated transaction, task, event or other typed record owns the domain fact. Corrections use the domain lifecycle and audit.
Derived presentationIndexes, dashboards, patterns, timeline views and caches refer to canonical sources and inherit privacy. They are rebuildable or versioned; they never replace financial or domain truth.

Extraction success cannot confirm an expense. A dashboard cache cannot become a ledger. Simulations remain separate overlays; promotion is an ordinary approved domain change.

Entity ownership and dictionary

Each entity has one authoritative owner. Views in other modules link to that identity. A profile supplies explicit lifecycle, privacy, synchronization, revision, retention, deletion and export rules; each catalog entry adds its fields, relationships and domain exceptions.

134 conceptual entities. Profiles below define the common behavior; entity-specific fields and exceptions remain authoritative.

Evidence lifecycle profile
DimensionContract
Lifecyclecaptured → persisted → verified; processing status is independent; archive/trash/purge follows retention and authorization.
PrivacySource policy applies; derivatives inherit restrictions.
SyncImmutable original blobs transfer separately with checksums; local/raw policy can prohibit transfer.
RevisionOriginal bytes are immutable; corrections or replacements create linked versions.
RetentionOwner-defined retention, reference-aware purge and backup-expiry disclosure.
DeletionAuthorized deletion propagates to derivatives/indexes and respects references and disclosed backup retention.
ExportOriginal bytes plus manifest, provenance, relationships and hashes.

DimensionContract

Data invariants

  • Store monetary amounts with exact decimal or integer minor-unit semantics; store currency alongside value. Do not aggregate currencies without a dated conversion basis.
  • Store instants in UTC with relevant timezone and local recurrence intent; test daylight-saving transitions and travel.
  • Maintain original observation units plus normalized values when conversions are valid; record timestamps and provenance.
  • Use stable IDs and unique source/external identifiers where available, schema versions, optimistic concurrency and explicit conflict resolution.
  • Avoid hard deletion of linked objects without confirmation; honor deletion policy, retention schedules, and cleanup of search/vector indexes and cached derivatives.
ARC-12P0Canonical domain ownership and evidence
Phase 01 · Platform · Web, Android, Server · Required · Not Verified

Objective: Use canonical domain records for domain calculations and decisions; link knowledge as evidence rather than silently converting inferred content into facts or duplicating monetary events.

Acceptance criteria (1)
  1. ARC-12-AC01 Approve one extracted expense, show it in two dashboards and inspect its receipt; there is one validated transaction, evidence remains separate and aggregate values reconcile.Evidence: not recorded

Prerequisites: ARC-01

Feasibility: Implementation and acceptance verification required; no external-provider dependency for the core manual behavior.

Applicable shared contracts: authorization, lifecycle, accessibility

Integration strategy

Integration category Initial capability Later / conditional capability
Calendars & contacts Manual import/export; calendar files. Scoped calendar sync, optional contact access; no broad inbox access by default.
Banking & investments Manual entry and CSV import. Region-appropriate read-only aggregators, market-data licensing, refresh and consent renewal.
Payments & billing Due dates, payment status and provider links. Approved provider handoff, webhooks and verified reconciliation; separate compliance review.
Health & wearables Manual tracking and supported exports. Platform health APIs and wearables, with per-data-type permission and source precedence.
Files & documents Upload, local import and portable export. Cloud storage connectors, OCR and owner-selected email/document ingestion.
Smart home & makers Manual device/project inventory. Home hub adapters, authenticated MQTT/device gateway, Raspberry Pi and Arduino SDK examples.
Weather & places Manual event context. Optional coarse location or owner-entered place for wardrobe/travel suggestions.
AI & automation Provider-abstracted inference and internal rules. Additional models, local inference, sandboxed webhooks and extension APIs.

Connector lifecycle

Connect → preview scopes → authorize → initial sync → incremental sync → review conflicts → disconnect. Use least-privilege credentials, encrypted token storage, revocation handling, backoff and versioned adapters. Explain whether disconnecting retains imported records; offer deletion where feasible. No connector should be required to use manual features.

Knowledge processing lifecycle

Lifecycle: captured → persisted → queued → extracted → indexed → ready (or partially indexed / failed); archived and trashed are independent of processing state. Revisions and original bytes are immutable; corrections generate new revisions/derivatives. Purge follows reference, retention and authorization checks and removes affected derivatives and indexes. Export manifest maps all IDs, original paths, relationships and checksums.

09 / Technical architecture

Single-owner self-hosted modular monolith, .NET 10 backend, Angular web and offline-first Expo Android.

No database or admin ports exposed to the internet. Encrypted backup copies on independent storage.

Remote access and authentication

  • Use Cloudflare Tunnel as the default no-VPN approach. Cloudflared initiates outbound connections, so no inbound router port forwarding or public IP is required. Bind origin services to loopback or a private container network. Cloudflare is a trusted HTTPS intermediary, not an end-to-end encrypted relay.
  • Proposed hostnames: {owner-domain} for Angular, api.{owner-domain} for authenticated native API and OIDC endpoints. A separate browser same-origin API route/BFF may forward internally; use explicit allowed origins and cookies with CSRF protection. Domain ownership is stated by the owner; DNS, certificates, tunnel and API hostname are proposed, not provisioned or verified.
  • Protect browser access using Cloudflare Access with an owner-only identity policy, plus application-level session authorization. Use a native-compatible OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE and system browser, short-lived access tokens, rotated refresh tokens, issuer/audience validation and SecureStore. Do not require an interactive Cloudflare Access cookie on native API calls; protect native API using application auth, rate limits and restrictive routing. Never embed permanent service tokens or client secrets in the APK.
  • Bootstrap the sole owner locally with a recovery procedure, MFA/passkey where supported, device/session registration and explicit scopes. Work Mode uses separate restricted sessions with server-side authorization; a browser toggle must not unlock sensitive data. Do not expose PostgreSQL, file storage, worker dashboard or host management publicly.
  • Home desktop and network must be available for remote access. LAN access may use a trusted local HTTPS origin with consistent auth and a documented certificate/DNS strategy; offline Android is the fallback, not remote failover.

Native capability strategy

Prefer Expo and React Native for the whole application, with Kotlin modules only when platform APIs require them. Health Connect access depends on data types, source app support, device availability and granular consent; complete Samsung Health data coverage is not assumed. S Pen and background execution need device-specific feasibility tests. Use native builds early and test the supported phone and stylus tablet.

Architecture decision status

ClassificationContract
Fixed architectureSingle owner, self-hosted home architecture, Android-first native client, online-first full web workspace, modular monolith, canonical domain ownership and one durable synchronization protocol.
Selected implementation direction.NET/ASP.NET Core, Angular/TypeScript, React Native/Expo, PostgreSQL, encrypted SQLite, generated typed contracts and protected original-file storage. Pin compatible versions during implementation.
Pending feasibility decisionsHost setup, identity packages, optional sync framework, rich-text/native ink approach, background scheduling, library versions, local models, backup targets and provider connectors. Decide with measured acceptance evidence, not document mention.

The product modules are logical business capabilities inside a modular monolith. They do not imply separate databases, deployments, UI frameworks or synchronization engines. Shared identity, policy, files, search, events, audit, notifications, analytics and AI orchestration implement common contracts.

For an unresolved choice, record an architecture decision with context, options, constraints, acceptance tests, selected outcome and evidence. A library mentioned as an evaluation candidate is not a mandatory dependency.

Use a modular monolith with vertical slices. Modules own their commands, invariants and database schemas. Use explicit interfaces, typed events and transactional outbox rather than cross-module table writes. A separate worker process may share the application assemblies; it is not a separate microservice architecture. Keep API contracts and generated types shared; do not attempt to share Angular/React UI components or duplicate canonical business rules in TypeScript.

Persistence and analytics

PostgreSQL is the canonical record store. Use schemas identity, core, productivity, finance, health, knowledge, inventory, lifestyle, analytics, automation, integrations, sync and audit. Use typed relational tables and a shared record registry with stable IDs for links, tags and attachments. Store binaries outside the database in a protected filesystem-backed object-store abstraction; use content hashes, metadata and reference counting. Do not assume hashes alone authorize access.

  • Analytics owns derived read models, SQL views, materialized aggregates, snapshots and metric definitions; refresh via outbox events and scheduled rebuilds. Keep source data and formulas traceable; do not store derived values as the only truth.
  • Support customizable date ranges, comparison periods, drill-downs, cross-domain filters, time-series charts, heatmaps, Sankey diagrams, portfolio treemaps and scenario forecasts. Use exact currency arithmetic and timezone-aware intervals.
  • Add PostgreSQL full-text search first; pgvector only for opted-in semantic retrieval; TimescaleDB or partitioning only if high-volume telemetry warrants it. Redis, Grafana, Ollama, MQTT and Home Assistant are optional later additions, not foundation dependencies.

API conventions

Versioned authenticated APIs; validation errors, pagination, cursor-based sync, idempotency, optimistic concurrency, scoped permissions, replay protection, signed webhooks, structured errors, rate limits and documented contracts. Never return raw connector credentials.

Knowledge architecture — designed from the foundation

Use the .NET 10 modular monolith, PostgreSQL canonical storage, Angular web and Expo Android shells. Add bounded Knowledge, Capture/Ingestion, Document Editing, Extraction, Retrieval and Copilot components within the defined module/service boundaries. Separate resource-intensive jobs from interactive request processing; no microservice fleet required.

Originals are authoritative; extracted text, vectors, previews and AI output are rebuildable or versioned derivatives.
Component Initial design / verification
Canonical editor model Versioned JSON block tree and vector stroke/geometry schema with stable IDs, page and canvas coordinate spaces; attachment IDs instead of embedded large bytes. Server validates payload sizes, schema versions and references. Renderers share document contracts, golden fixtures and compatibility tests, not necessarily UI code.
Rich text engine Evaluate a ProseMirror-family web editor and Android-compatible editor bridge or native alternative. Test IME, selection, keyboard, tables, accessibility, large documents and offline editing before committing. Sanitize imported HTML and prohibit executable embeds.
Native Android ink Dedicated Kotlin view / Expo native module for stylus input, event batching, pressure/tilt, palm rejection and rendering; avoid per-point JavaScript bridge traffic. Consider Android low-latency graphics APIs subject to device and SDK validation; export portable vector strokes.
Web ink and canvas Pointer events and vector/canvas renderer with viewport culling, device pixel ratio handling and common geometry; evaluate canvas library options with large-document and accessibility tests. Web stylus capabilities depend on the hardware and browser.
PDF and media Evaluate PDF.js on web and a compatible Android renderer with independent annotation layer; isolate media decoding and document conversion. Preserve original bytes and page/time anchors.
Capture API and file storage Resumable chunked uploads with upload session ID, expected length/hash, final verification, atomic attachment link and cleanup of abandoned uploads. Range reads for permitted large media; private storage paths never publicly accessible.
Extract and index workers Outbox queues, bounded concurrency, sandboxed MIME-specific parsers, OCR/handwriting/ASR provider adapters; checkpoints, retry/backoff and dead-letter review. No extraction task changes the original.
Search PostgreSQL FTS + indexed metadata and optional trigram matching; pgvector for approved semantic retrieval; per-revision chunks and evidence anchors. Add dedicated search infrastructure only after measured need.
Copilot gateway Provider abstraction, local or permitted remote models, retrieval authorization, prompt isolation, grounded answers, typed proposals, citations and owner budgets. Evaluate hardware and model quality before choosing providers.
Desktop capture helper Optional cross-platform .NET utility or equivalent native packaging; enrolled narrowly scoped upload identity, OS-protected credentials, approved directory roots, explicit exclusions, local spool and revocation. No broad filesystem access from web.
Export / interop Versioned JSON manifest + original blobs + readable Markdown/HTML, PDF and SVG where applicable; annotated PDF copies. Document format capability matrix; preserve unsupported fields and explicitly report lossy conversions.

Proposed interfaces and deployment boundaries

Interface / process Responsibility
POST /api/v1/captures; /uploads Capture envelopes, idempotency, resumable uploads and status.
/api/v1/knowledge/items; /revisions; /annotations Record metadata, versioned editor operations, PDF and canvas layers; authorization and optimistic concurrency.
/api/v1/imports; /connectors; /watch-roots Preview, batch import, progress, source scopes, checkpoints and disconnect.
/api/v1/search; /copilot; /proposals Authorized lexical/hybrid results, evidence-backed answers, review/undo.
Shared /sync endpoints + SignalR Durable operation protocol; realtime invalidation only, not transport of authoritative writes.
Compose service profiles API/web, PostgreSQL, cloudflared, durable worker, blob volumes and backup; optional isolated extraction/model workers; resource limits and independent health checks.

These are proposed component contracts, not a completed detailed engineering design. Exact endpoint schemas, document operations, migration SQL, editor SDKs, native latency, identity routing and hardware sizing are phase-01 architecture decision records and prototypes. Do not commit to a library or provider without compatibility, licensing, quality and recovery tests.

Shared knowledge and structured-data architecture

Use the modular monolith and canonical PostgreSQL model. Structured domain data and Knowledge share storage, provenance, links, permissions, search, analytics and AI infrastructure. Domain facts stay in typed authoritative tables; Knowledge supplies originals, documents and evidence. Shared capability does not require extra services or duplicate storage.

Platform decisions and portability

Portability concern SaveSphere binding direction
Android UI and local schema tooling Use Expo mobile and native capabilities. Encrypted SQLite is mandatory; evaluate Drizzle for local schema tooling without creating independent server schema authority.
API implementation and schema validation Implement domain APIs and schema validation in .NET 10/ASP.NET Core with generated contracts. Share framework-neutral TypeScript utilities where appropriate.
Relational storage and data isolation Use self-hosted canonical PostgreSQL. Preserve defense-in-depth data isolation, least-privilege service roles and privacy checks; no second database.
PowerSync Evaluate against the durable synchronization contracts; adopt only if self-hostable and passes all conflict, privacy and recovery tests. Otherwise use the specified synchronization protocol. No dual active sync engines.
Job scheduling and optional caching Use the shared .NET durable scheduler/jobs. Redis is optional when measurements justify it; job semantics are independent of that infrastructure choice.
File and object storage Use self-hosted file/object storage with typed media, ACLs, integrity and scoped export links.
Server-side AI The shared SaveSphere AI gateway, optional local server inference. No direct client provider keys.
Web management and administration Full Angular workspace already mandatory.
Future iOS P2 conditional platform extension; preserve portable domain and adapter boundaries.

10 / Privacy & security

Trust is a core product requirement, especially when financial, health, journal, home and identity data live together.

Independent privacy dimensions

Independent dimensionValues / policy
SensitivityStandard, private, sensitive.
Storage scopeDevice-only or explicitly permitted server synchronization.
Lock requirementAuthorized normal session or fresh sensitive unlock.
Processing modeRaw-only or approved processing.
AI eligibilityExcluded, retrieval allowed or explicitly approved processing; model confidence grants no authority.
Search visibilityHidden, authorized lexical or authorized semantic; scope before ranking.
Dashboard exposureHidden, generic/redacted or authorized content.
Notification exposureNone, generic/redacted or authorized content.
AI memory, summaries and correlationsIndependent purpose-specific permissions; excluded sources cannot leak through derived results.
Export eligibilityExcluded or explicit scoped export approval, with unlock where required.
Evaluation consentDenied by default or separately opted in with version, purpose, revocation and retention.

Do not implement privacy as one enum containing sensitivity, storage location and lock state. Capture presets compile into the dimensions below. A separate permission is needed to relax any applicable restriction; derived outputs inherit the strictest source policy.

Privacy and security controls

Control Required behavior
Data ownership & consent Provide a readable data inventory, module-level opt-in, purpose-specific permissions, export, correction, deletion, and revocation. No advertising, public accounts, or sale of personal data.
Authentication Locally bootstrap one owner; enforce strong authentication, MFA/passkey where supported, recovery, device/session management, rate limits and reauthentication for sensitive changes.
Authorization Deny by default; enforce owner, enrolled session/device, purpose, record, connector, AI and automation scopes at the server. Work Mode is a restricted credential/session, not a visual filter.
Encryption Encrypt transport, host disks, Android SQLite and backups; protect keys independently, use platform secure storage for local credentials and limit service filesystem access. Evaluate optional client-side encrypted vaults, with explicit search/AI trade-offs.
Sensitive content Private defaults for journal, health and financial records; prevent sensitive previews in lock-screen notifications and exclude such payloads from telemetry by default.
AI processing Explain processing location, provider access and retention. Do not use personal content for model training without separate explicit opt-in; verify vendor terms and settings before enabling processing.
Data lifecycle Define retention for logs, files, backups and AI artifacts; implement deletion of live data, derived indexes and caches; disclose backup expiration and legal-retention exceptions.
Audit & integrity Record security-sensitive actions, permissions, external effects and rule execution; protect audit logs from tampering and inappropriate content exposure.
Recovery & incident response Test restores, document incident handling and escalation, provide owner notifications when required, and establish dependency/vulnerability management.
Sharing & portability Private-by-default sharing, revocable permissions and clear audience previews; structured JSON/CSV, readable Markdown and original attachments where applicable.

Safety by domain

  • Financial: display estimates and assumptions; avoid guarantees or personalized trade execution. Payment functionality is gated by legal, provider and security review.
  • Health and nutrition: wellness information is not diagnosis or treatment; avoid unsafe recommendations, extreme restriction and medication dosing. Provide appropriate guidance to seek qualified or emergency help when relevant, without implying monitoring or rescue.
  • Mood and journaling: avoid diagnostic labeling, guilt-based engagement and unsolicited sensitive analysis. Owners control whether and how reflection features are enabled.
  • Smart home: no covert monitoring, bypassing access controls or unsupervised safety-critical actuation. Use allowlisted devices and commands, verified state, owner override, and fail-safe behavior.
  • Work-device access: no financial, journal, health, private document or administrative data on restricted work sessions; disable persistent API caching, redact notifications, apply no-store headers and explicitly allowlist records.

Personal-use security and integration readiness

No commercial launch or regulated-service claim is planned. Threat-model the home server, tunnel, credentials, stolen devices, offline replicas, connectors and AI retrieval. Verify applicable provider terms, API availability, licensing, consent and data handling before connecting finance, health or other sensitive services. Do not claim compliance or end-to-end encryption without validation.

Device access and recovery

  • Full access only for approved personal sessions. Work credentials have allowlisted modules, short sessions, no offline records, no service worker data caching and no administration; browser/endpoint monitoring remains outside SaveSphere control.
  • Revocation stops future authorized server reads and sync. Offline copies cannot be remotely guaranteed erased until a device reconnects; use local encrypted storage, app lock, expiry policy and documented lost-device handling.
  • Redact private values in logs and notifications; exclude sensitive modules from AI and general search unless specifically enabled. Derived metrics inherit relevant restrictions.
  • Keep recovery codes and encryption keys off the host. Test owner recovery, device revocation, key rotation, encrypted restore and rollback before trusting the platform with irreplaceable data.
  • Offer an owner-generated emergency recovery package (SEC-10) for the case where the home server is inaccessible. It is encrypted, opens without SaveSphere, keeps its key off the host and out of the package, excludes highly private domains by default, and is verified by hash and by a periodic owner restore test. It supplements, and does not replace, the encrypted backups above.

Emergency access and recovery

SEC-10P0 · proposed priorityEmergency recovery package
Phase 01 · Platform · Web, Android, Server · Required · Not Verified

Objective: Let the owner generate an encrypted, self-contained recovery package so essential information stays reachable if the home server becomes inaccessible.

Functional contract

The owner selects the contents from a checklist that includes emergency contacts, critical document locations and masked identifiers, account and provider inventory, bill and obligation schedule, insurance and medical essentials, access and recovery instructions, and server restore and re-enrollment steps. Highly private domains, such as private journal, spiritual reflection and private review, are excluded unless explicitly included. The package opens without SaveSphere, the server or an AI provider, using documented open formats and a human-readable index, and an optional printable summary. Encryption keys and recovery codes are never stored on the host or inside the same package. Each package records its generation time, content manifest and hashes. SaveSphere warns when a package is stale and reminds the owner to refresh it and to test it. Generation and each export are audit-logged.

Acceptance criteria (1)
  1. SEC-10-AC01 With the server stopped, the owner opens a package on a clean device using only the documented format and key, and finds the essential records and restore instructions. A tampered or truncated package fails hash verification. An excluded private domain contains no data in the package.Evidence: not recorded

Prerequisites: ARC-01, SEC-01, SEC-05

Feasibility: Implementation and acceptance verification required; no external-provider dependency for the core manual behavior.

Applicable shared contracts: authorization, lifecycle, accessibility, deterministic core

Privacy and data rules for derived views. The timeline, relationship explorer, decision journal, simulations, emergency recovery package, data-health dashboard and historical views operate on canonical source records and do not introduce another life-data store or a new domain. Each reads through shared authorization: Work Mode, domain privacy, sensitive unlock and AI exclusions apply as in the source module, and derived views inherit the strictest restriction of their inputs. “All authorized domains” means only domains the current session may read; hidden records and their counts must not be disclosed. These capabilities remain usable without an AI provider and supplement their owning modules without replacing requirements or downgrading priorities.

Knowledge-specific privacy and preservation

  • Treat all imports as untrusted: validate MIME and size, defend against archive expansion, malformed PDFs, macros, active HTML, unsafe URLs and parser resource exhaustion. Isolate extraction with no ambient secrets and restricted network/filesystem permissions.
  • Owner-selected and explicitly authorized import only. Exclude credentials, secrets, restricted employer files and private third-party content beyond lawful personal use. Fetch permitted web content only; enforce URL fetch allowlists/SSRF controls, size and redirect limits.
  • Original blobs are immutable while retained. Use encrypted disk and backups, integrity scrubs, reference-aware purge, deletion propagation, and backup retention disclosure. An optional client-encrypted vault cannot support normal server-side indexing unless explicitly unlocked for that purpose.
  • Enforce scope checks for search results, counts, facets, snippets, source previews, thumbnails, exports, AI evidence, embeddings and derived summaries. Revocation invalidates access and requests local purge when a device next connects; remote erasure of an offline/stolen device is not guaranteed.
  • Do not persist sensitive content in telemetry, crash reports, push notifications or work-browser caches. Require explicit external inference consent and disclose provider processing/retention; allow local-only or AI-disabled items.
  • Backup manifests include database, originals, revisions, annotations and relationship integrity. Indexes and previews can be rebuilt; ensure restore exercises also verify a representative ink note, PDF annotations and external import.

Capture privacy matrix — default behavior

Mode Sync AI / memory Search & display Review
Normal Eligible by domain consent Eligible by explicit scope Normal authorized surfaces Normal
Private Only opted-in No by default; separate permission Locked private surfaces Sensitive unlock
Local-only Blocked Blocked for the capture pipeline Hidden ordinary search Locked local
Exclude from AI Local by default; explicit non-AI archival policy may permit future sync Blocked including embeddings, transcription and memory Private/manual retrieval only by default Sensitive unlock
Do not analyze Blocked Blocked: no processing of any kind No indexing, summary, dashboard or ordinary search Locked raw-only

Privacy dimensions may restrict these defaults further. Export is an explicit scoped operation, never a bypass for Work Mode or an automatic upload. Local-only records cannot enter the server AI pipeline; even optional on-device inference requires an explicit separate policy change for a raw-only item.

Failure behavior

FailureRequired behavior
Insufficient storageDo not acknowledge an unsaved item. Explain required space and preserve already committed local records; retries must not duplicate accepted effects.
Server or network unavailablePersist supported local mutations and show pending/stale state. Network-only features remain explicitly unavailable.
Permission revoked or credentials expiredStop newly disallowed reads, processing and upload. Reauthenticate when appropriate without losing permitted pending work; do not replay under stale authority.
Concurrent editPreserve conflicting versions, expose resolution and apply the domain’s approved merge policy. No silent overwrite of pending edits.
App kill, reboot or background limitsCommitted records, files and operations survive; schedules rebuild where supported. OS scheduling limitations are visible.
Partial upload or index failureOriginal and processing states remain separate; retry derivatives and transfers using stable identities and checksums.

Offline-first Android and durable synchronization

Read and write supported data in encrypted SQLite. A local transaction saves the record and an outbox operation together. The UI shows pending, syncing, synced, conflict or failed status. Server changes are pulled incrementally; SignalR merely signals that new changes exist. A killed app or reboot must not erase pending operations.

Capability Offline behavior
Tasks, checklists, habits, manual expenses, workouts, journal Create, edit and complete locally; sync later.
Calendar and routines Full for downloaded/local records; external calendar changes await connectivity.
Notes, inventory, wardrobe Read and edit downloaded records; missing attachments clearly marked.
Receipt/document capture Persist file locally and queue upload; local extraction only if implemented.
Dashboards Cached or locally computed subsets with freshness/completeness indicators.
Prices, AI, connectors Last-known prices; network-dependent operations unavailable or visibly queued.
IoT and external side effects Require reachable authorized gateway; no queued success or blind replay.

Synchronization protocol

  • Generate stable client IDs and operation IDs; associate device ID, entity type, base server version, payload schema version and operation intent. Use a server-side deduplication receipt table with unique operation IDs.
  • Push validated mutations in bounded batches, returning per-operation accepted/duplicate/conflict/invalid outcomes and versions. Apply each logical write, change journal entry and outbox event atomically.
  • Pull by opaque server-issued monotonically ordered cursor over committed changes; use a consistent bootstrap snapshot and watermark. Do not rely on client timestamps for ordering. Handle expired cursors with safe rebootstrap while preserving pending writes.
  • Apply inbound changes and cursor updates in a single local transaction. Keep tombstones until retention/acknowledgement rules permit purge; clean up caches on scope revocation.
  • Preserve simultaneous edits as conflict versions; allow review and merge for notes, explicit resolution for financial records, and deterministic domain-specific merging only where safe. Never silently overwrite pending work.
  • Sync files separately using resumable or retryable uploads, content verification and authenticated metadata; preserve unresolved local files until confirmed.
  • Sync on launch, resume, foreground network recovery, manual refresh and opportunistic background runs. Android WorkManager periodic scheduling is inexact (minimum interval typically 15 minutes); battery management may delay execution. Use local reminders independent of server access. 
POST /api/v1/sync/push
GET  /api/v1/sync/pull?cursor=<opaque-cursor>
GET  /api/v1/sync/status

Knowledge sync and conflict design

  • Use current operation IDs, outbox, canonical versions and pull cursors. Store local note/ink/canvas operations and pending file payloads durably before confirming capture. Encrypt local files in addition to SQLite; protect keys via platform storage.
  • Separate note text, stroke/object, annotation and metadata edits into stable-ID operations; merge independent additions only when deterministic. Concurrent edits of the same object or deletion-vs-edit preserve both versions and expose review. Do not silently apply last-write-wins.
  • Begin with optimistic concurrency, operation batches, snapshots and conflict UI. Evaluate CRDTs only if actual concurrent editing needs justify the added persistence, tombstone and migration complexity.
  • A note may sync before a large attachment finishes. Represent pending/missing blobs explicitly; finalize only after server checksum validation. Sync metadata before derivatives; clients can read original content even if indexing fails.
  • Version canonical schemas from phase 01; test backward compatibility, lossless serialization, export/import and migration on old fixtures. Keep supported client versions safe through negotiated capabilities and documented support windows.

12 / Quality & acceptance

Verification model

LayerWhat it verifies
Requirement acceptanceIndividual behavior through identified AC entries and implementation evidence.
Domain invariantsMoney, schedules, observation units, lifecycle and canonical ownership.
Shared platform contractsAuthorization, privacy, synchronization, durability, audit and deletion.
Non-functional targetsMeasured performance, recovery, accessibility, reliability and cost.
Connected workflowsEnd-to-end behavior across permitted domains without duplicated facts.
Release acceptanceThe increment’s scope, conditions, defects, restore/rollback and owner acceptance.

AI-independent operation

Timeline, Relationship Explorer, Decision Journal, simulations, emergency recovery packages, Data Health and historical views remain usable without an AI provider. Their canonical data, deterministic calculations, manual actions and required safety checks do not depend on inference. Optional narrative or suggestions cannot become a prerequisite or override source facts.

AI-08, M01-R22, ARC-12

Authorization and derived-data scope

Check owner, enrolled device/session, domain, purpose and current policy before reads and actions. Derived views inherit the strictest source restriction; denied records and counts are absent.

SEC-01, AI-01, KN-26

Independent privacy policy

Evaluate storage, processing, unlock, AI, visibility and consent independently. Raw-only/local-only content never enters ordinary upload or processing; recheck policy at execution and persistence.

SEC-01, SEC-02, SEC-03, SEC-08

Capability-specific offline behavior

Apply the Offline & Synchronization capability matrix. Acknowledge only durable supported writes; show unavailable, pending, conflict and retry states accurately.

ARC-02, ARC-03, NFR-06

Identity, provenance and lifecycle

Separate immutable evidence, proposed interpretation, confirmed records and derived views. Use stable identities, versions, deletion propagation and portable export.

ARC-01, ARC-12, SEC-09, KN-02

Idempotency and audit

Use stable operation IDs, record meaningful state transitions, redact private payloads and compensate reversible actions without erasing history.

ARC-02, NFR-05, AIP-06

Accessibility and interaction states

Support keyboard and equivalent native access, labels, text resizing, contrast, reduced motion and non-color-only status. Verify empty, loading, error, denied, locked, offline, stale and retry states where applicable.

NFR-08, QA-09

Shared AI authority

Models propose typed outputs under current policy. Approval is action-specific; confidence never elevates authority. Deterministic calculations and manual core workflows survive inference outage.

AI-03, AI-04, AI-06, AIP-02, AIP-03

Financial integrity

Use exact amounts and explicit currencies, dated conversion assumptions and canonical transactions. Transfers, views and retries do not double-count money or imply payment.

M05-R02, ARC-12, NFR-05

Sensitive-domain behavior

Apply private defaults and owner consent, protect previews and third-party context, and avoid diagnostic, coercive or guilt-based interpretations.

SEC-04, SEC-06, QA-02

One test may supply evidence for several linked requirements and invariants when it proves their complete conditions. Reuse versioned fixtures and evidence references instead of maintaining duplicate tests. Specialist gates are linked to the requirements they verify in the register.

Testing strategy

  • Unit tests for recurrence, timezones, financial arithmetic, transfer pairing, unit conversions and rule conditions.
  • Integration and contract tests for imports, connectors, revocation, authorization, payment status and device acknowledgement; use mocks/sandboxes for risky actions.
  • End-to-end tests for owner bootstrap, enrollment, capture, search, planning, reconciliation, journal exclusion, exports, offline sync and device revocation and complete export.
  • Adversarial AI and privacy tests for prompt injection, cross-device scope and cross-module data leakage, incorrect citations, fabricated actions and unsafe recommendations.
  • Accessibility, localization, performance, reliability, backup restore and regression testing on a defined device/browser matrix.

Release gates

Each increment passes the acceptance criteria assigned to its declared scope and all applicable shared contracts. Core product acceptance includes its P0 requirements; intermediate vertical slices do not imply that unfinished scope is delivered. Core manual flows work without AI. The owner verifies privacy, security, consent, deletion, monitoring, rollback and backup recovery. No unresolved data-loss, permission-bypass or high-severity security defect is accepted as a normal release condition.

Distributed-system verification matrix

Test Expected outcome
Airplane mode, app kill, reboot Local record, file and queued operation survive; sync resumes later.
Same operation retried after response lost One canonical change and no repeated financial or rule effects.
Phone and tablet edit same record concurrently Conflict is preserved and visible; no silent loss.
Server reboot, tunnel outage, expired cursor Clients surface unavailable/stale status; recovery preserves local mutations.
Work session / revoked device Sensitive API routes and records are denied, even if queried directly.
Restore to spare host or VM Database, attachments and relationships reconcile; secrets recovered separately.
Performance / UI Desktop, both laptops, work desktop and both Android screen sizes tested; reduced motion and keyboard interaction supported.

Proposed scale test fixtures

Test at least 50,000 searchable records initially, then add synthetic multi-year transactions, health observations, events, documents and dashboard queries. Measure on actual hardware rather than introducing distributed infrastructure prematurely.
