Additional measurable targets (proposals, not benchmarks)

Target Verification
Offline capture Meet the KN capture target; structured text and template capture durable within 1 second p95 on representative devices, excluding large media copy.
Daily State / recovery Deterministic Today computation within 500 ms p95 on representative local dataset; recovery preview within 2 s for a typical day. No forced model call.
Privacy Zero known unauthorized raw/private leakage across automated fixtures; no sensitive values in operational logs.
Import integrity 100% source records accounted for as imported, matched, skipped by owner or quarantined; all eligible media hashes match; zero unexplained loss.
Notifications No duplicate logical notification per occurrence/version in controlled tests; OS limitations documented.
Deterministic analytics Exact agreement for counts and currency minor-unit arithmetic across query, dashboard, export and review fixtures.
Test fixture scale Extend the 50,000-record fixtures with mixed Deen, health, relationship, review and capture histories over multiple years; include restricted device, local-only and conflicting edits.

Product success measures

Measure utility, integrity, reliability and engineering progress—not owner growth or commercial retention.

Metric Measurement / proposed target
Weekly personal usefulness At least one completed planning/review loop per week; review whether SaveSphere actually replaces fragmented tools.
Capture efficiency Median simple expense/task/note capture within 15 seconds on the phone, using repeatable personal tests.
Cross-device integrity 100% of critical retry, conflict, offline persistence and device-scope tests pass; zero known silent data loss.
Synchronization latency Measure time from foreground reconnection to convergence; initial target ≤ 10 seconds for a small pending batch on a healthy network.
Cross-domain usefulness At least one intentional linked workflow used regularly, such as purchase-to-inventory or goal-to-habit.
Dashboard correctness Aggregates reconcile to source records; missing data, freshness, currency and assumptions visible.
Recovery readiness Encrypted backup age and restore checks within configured RPO/RTO; test isolated restoration periodically.
Automation reliability Target ≥ 99% verified successful supported internal runs; report failures and duplicate effects separately.
AI grounded accuracy (knowledge release and later) Target ≥ 95% on a representative owner-reviewed evaluation set; zero known permission leakage.
Operational health Track availability, failed jobs, resource consumption, disk capacity, inference costs and unresolved security defects.

Measurement guardrails

All targets are proposed acceptance criteria, not measured performance. Use local telemetry with minimal metadata, no sensitive payloads and no third-party tracking by default. Avoid compulsive streaks or excessive notification volume. Reassess metrics after actual use.

Knowledge success measures

Metric Proposed measurement
Capture friction One share action plus optional metadata; median ≤15 s for everyday capture including launch. Track failed or abandoned saves.
Import coverage 100% of input export items accounted for as imported, duplicate, skipped or failed; original checksum verification where bytes are available.
Retrievability Owner-authored benchmark of known saved items and natural-language recall queries; measure success in top results and time to evidence.
Authoring replacement Track whether typed, ink and PDF daily workflows can be completed without leaving SaveSphere for supported workflows; record unmet cases.
Rediscovery value Owner feedback on relevant resurfaced items, dismiss rate, frequency limits and opt-out use.
Archive integrity Zero known lost originals, unresolved silent conflicts or unauthorized access; successful restore and portable export tests.

Product success measures

Metric Proposed measurement
Command-center usefulness Track whether Today supports an actionable daily overview and regular review across enabled domains; record missing or unhelpful widgets.
Life-domain utility Track actual use of released domain workflows and whether each replaces fragmented tools; distinguish disabled, not-yet-built and blocked modules.
Knowledge utility Retain all Knowledge success measures; evaluate authoring and retrieval separately from dashboard use.
Cross-domain evidence value Owner-reviewed examples of notes, receipts, manuals or saved research supporting a structured decision or action without duplicated facts.
Balanced delivery Review the register at each milestone: completed, pending, blocked and explicitly deferred requirements by module/priority; no silent removals or downgrades.
Non-AI continuity Regularly verify the owner can plan, capture, edit supported notes, review dashboards and manage structured records during inference outages.

Additional personal success measures

Measure Interpretation
Capture friction Time to durable save; fraction of drafts resolved without repeated prompts; correction effort, no incentive to overlog.
Recovery usefulness Owner-rated feasibility of recovered plans and accepted versus dismissed suggestions; no life score.
Relationship follow-up Opt-in completion and overdue follow-ups, not relationship quality or moral rating.
Deen Private owner-selected progress, unlogged separate, no ranking or guilt.
Trust Zero unexplained import loss, duplicate expenses, unauthorized disclosures; successful offline restore and exports.
Intelligence usefulness Evidence coverage, correction rate, accepted suggestions and reminder suppression; owner can disable measurement.

13 / Development roadmap

Eight phases, incremental domain delivery and explicit release evidence. Target phases are planning decisions independent of priority.

Unified phase plan

01 · Platform foundation

Goal: Establish secure, recoverable product foundations.

Foundation contracts from: No prior phase

Deliverables
  • Monorepo, .NET 10 API, PostgreSQL, Angular/Expo shells, Docker Compose, Cloudflare, owner auth, device scopes, design tokens, backups and generated contracts. Define canonical knowledge/ink/canvas schema, storage manifest, extraction boundaries, desktop/web route and early S Pen/editor/import feasibility spikes. Delivery dependency: SEC-10 emergency recovery package is P0 and ships with phase 01 backup and recovery verification, with content classes added as each domain lands.
  • Threat model, document schema, editor/ink prototypes, representative import corpus, permission model and storage/recovery proof.
  • Stable typed IDs, independent privacy policy, local authentication and lock, per-entity synchronization strategies, capture state machine, event log and representative import fixtures. Establish the expense and Knowledge vertical-slice test plans.
Feasibility and vertical-slice proofs
  • M09-R05: Canonical editor/ink schema and native feasibility prototypes.
  • ARC-11: Define import manifest/mapping contracts and representative format fixtures; complete adapters target Phase 06.
  • KN-10: Prototype stylus input, palm rejection, portable strokes and measured latency on the profile devices.
Exit criteria
  • Deploy reproducibly; personal browser reaches home server remotely without VPN; Android enrolls; backup and recovery verified. Architecture decisions, schema fixtures and native ink prototype reviewed.
  • Foundation contracts validate raw/local-only exclusion and authorization before sensitive workflows are enabled.
  • All requirements assigned to the released increment have acceptance evidence; privacy, source integrity, backup/restore and rollback are verified. Conditional or unfinished work is explicitly recorded, never represented as delivered.

  • Ramadan/khatam, Zakat, deload/progress photos, broader bank/wearables, advanced coach, optional iOS/HealthKit and deferred connector enhancements.
Exit criteria
  • Permission and prompt-injection tests pass; every side effect is bounded, idempotent and auditable. IoT actions require acknowledged state. Advanced features do not regress knowledge durability or permission boundaries.
  • Each feasibility gate documented; no placeholder described as delivered.
  • All requirements assigned to the released increment have acceptance evidence; privacy, source integrity, backup/restore and rollback are verified. Conditional or unfinished work is explicitly recorded, never represented as delivered.

Incremental delivery policy

DEL-01P1Independent domain delivery
Phase 01 · Delivery · Development · Required · Not Verified

Objective: Ship usable domain increments independently of unrelated advanced editor or ingestion work after shared foundations and applicable gates are met; report blocked dependencies rather than treating the whole Knowledge release as a prerequisite for every life domain.

Acceptance criteria (1)
  1. DEL-01-AC01 With an unrelated advanced editor blocked, release an independently complete domain slice after its own prerequisites and quality gates pass; the blocked capability remains tracked.Evidence: not recorded

Prerequisites: GOV-01

Feasibility: No provider gate. Requires an owner-approved register, explicit dependency decisions and documented delivery evidence.

Applicable shared contracts: authorization, lifecycle, accessibility

Deliver useful domain slices after their prerequisites and applicable gates pass. Phase dependencies identify foundation contracts, not a requirement to complete every feature in a prior phase. Requirement-level dependencies govern each increment; analytics can proceed when its source records and metric contracts are ready without waiting on unrelated editors or imports. Expense and hybrid-note vertical slices prove structured and document durability in the foundation period. Record a dependency owner, release scope and status for each increment.

First usable vertical slice

  • Record an expense on the supported Android phone in airplane mode; persist the record and operation atomically.
  • Force-close the application, reopen it, and verify the amount, currency, category, time and pending status.
  • Reconnect and synchronize with the home desktop; retry the same mutation without creating a duplicate transaction.
  • Update the Angular financial dashboard through SignalR invalidation and a fresh query.
  • Access the same dashboard from the personal laptop outside the home network, without a VPN client.
  • Read/edit the same transaction on the supported Android stylus tablet; test concurrent edits and visible resolution.
  • Verify work sessions cannot retrieve financial records; restore the slice from encrypted backup.

Critical dependencies

  • Identity, device scopes, canonical records, audit and backup precede sensitive domains.
  • Durable synchronization precedes widespread mobile writes.
  • Task/calendar primitives precede renewals, maintenance and learning schedules.
  • Financial reconciliation precedes recurring-charge inference, net worth and projections.
  • Provenance and permission-filtered search precede semantic retrieval and cross-domain analytics.
  • Safe rules, reliable jobs and connector isolation precede external actions and IoT.

Release readiness

Every release verifies its assigned requirements, cross-domain workflows, privacy, offline behavior, original-data integrity, export, restoration and rollback. Reconcile input records and hashes for supported imports. Record owner acceptance, defects, conditional gates and deferred work. A mapping or completed prototype alone is not evidence that a feature is delivered.

Automatic trading, unsafe medical or device actions, public marketplace and commercial multi-tenancy are out of scope. Conditional iOS, external providers, advanced local inference and other extensions follow their recorded feasibility gates; required later work is deferred rather than implicitly optional.

Major risks and mitigations

Risk Mitigation
Scope explosion Build shared primitives once; ship usable vertical slices; maintain a deferred backlog.
Offline data loss Atomic outbox, stable IDs, change journal, version checks, conflict UI and recovery tests.
Single-host failure Automatic startup, independent encrypted backups, restore rehearsals and offline Android fallback.
Home workstation contention Separate environments, resource limits, idle scheduling and storage monitoring.
Public ingress / sensitive data Private origin network, strong owner authentication, least-privilege sessions, Work Mode, rate limits and revocation.
AI hallucinations / unauthorized effects Scoped retrieval, typed tools, preview, approval, idempotency, evaluations and manual fallback.
Financial / health inaccuracies Exact arithmetic, provenance, uncertainty, source freshness, explicit assumptions and domain constraints.
Android limits / connector compatibility Early development builds, device-specific spikes, manual fallback, no guaranteed background execution or complete Samsung Health coverage.
Vendor cost or dependency Provider abstractions, local export and restore, usage budgets; avoid optional services until measured need.

Resolved decisions

Decision Selected direction
Audience One owner / developer / operator; no public registration, tenant or household accounts.
Platform Angular browser; Android via React Native + Expo, targeted Kotlin; .NET 10 backend.
Hosting Home desktop as canonical production host; no public SaaS; remote access via authenticated HTTPS tunnel.
Offline Android local-first SQLite with encrypted cache, durable sync and visible conflict handling; web online-first.
Architecture Modular monolith, vertical slices, relational PostgreSQL, background jobs and shared contracts.
UX Dark-first, bold domain colors, animated analytics and layouts tailored to desktop, phone and tablet.
Commercial scope No monetization, paid tiers, customer support or consumer launch KPIs.

Open implementation decisions

Decision Proposed default / verification needed
Host operating environment Windows assumed; verify actual OS, hardware, available disk, boot behavior, WSL2 vs dedicated Linux VM and service recovery.
Domain routing and identity Owner domain is {owner-domain}; validate DNS, Cloudflare Access plus native OIDC routing, identity provider and recovery method.
Library versions Pin mutually compatible .NET 10, EF/Npgsql, Hangfire storage, Angular and Expo releases after small build spikes; validate native integrations.
Backup targets Choose independent local storage and encrypted off-site destination; validate RPO/RTO and key custody.
Sync retention Choose tombstone retention, cursor expiry, device rebootstrap and per-domain merge semantics.
AI and connectors Select later based on privacy, API availability, cost, licensing and host capacity; manual fallback always available.
Data capture scope Choose first expense fields and import formats; decide downloaded record subsets, attachment quotas and privacy rules for each device.

Definition of done

A requirement is done only when its acceptance criteria, domain invariants, authorization, offline behavior where applicable, error states, accessibility, redacted telemetry, export/deletion, documentation and automated tests are verified by the owner. Deployment and recovery must be repeatable. No claim that a feature is implemented is made by this specification.

Product outcome

SaveSphere succeeds when a single owner can manage and understand life across the enrolled devices, while retaining control of the data, infrastructure and decisions—and can continue extending the system as a developer for years. Success also means everyday notes and saved knowledge are captured once, preserved with evidence and found without recalling their original app or location. SaveSphere succeeds when the owner can rely on the command center for everyday life management and on Knowledge for daily authoring and recall, with neither side requiring the other to be fully built before it provides value.

Knowledge architecture decisions and risks

Decision / risk Proposed disposition
Domain Use {owner-domain} for the full private web workspace; api.{owner-domain} proposed for native API/OIDC. Confirm DNS/Cloudflare access and recovery before exposure.
Desktop packaging Full Angular web/PWA first; optional narrowly scoped desktop helper for watched folders and capture. No full native Windows/Linux UI committed yet.
Import fidelity Collect representative owner exports; verify metadata, ink and layout conversion. Preserve source bytes and report any losses; no promise of complete proprietary-editor fidelity.
Connector availability Verify APIs, tenant permissions, terms and scopes individually. Share/export/file import remains fallback; no requirement depends on unsupported live social ingestion.
Host resources Measure storage volume, video sizes, OCR/ASR throughput, local model capability and restore cost; choose quotas, queue priorities and hardware based on evidence.
Editor choice Evaluate Android native stylus pipeline and rich-text bridge; canonical portable schema precedes library adoption. Test cross-device rendering, IME, accessibility and round trips.
AI privacy Local-first preference for sensitive data where viable, explicit remote processing permissions and per-item controls; choose models based on measured evidence quality and cost.
Architectural completeness Document full module boundaries, storage, sync, permissions, APIs and phased delivery before feature expansion. Detailed contracts and ADRs still require phase-01 spikes; no implementation or benchmark has been completed.

Product design decisions

Decision Selected direction
Identity Intelligence-driven personal operating system; dashboard-first full-personal desktop experience; Knowledge is a first-class workspace and shared engine.
Device emphasis Dashboard-first home desktop, balanced personal laptop, capture/action-first phone, Knowledge/Plan-first tablet and restricted productivity-first work computers. Owner-adjustable within authorization.
Architecture Canonical structured domain state plus shared knowledge, provenance, search, analytics and AI infrastructure. No new service split required.
Scope protection All defined modules and 302 indexed requirements remain in scope: 201 module requirements and 101 specialist, platform, quality or delivery requirements. Preserve all eight main phases, six Knowledge gates, seven integration gates and 22 implementation epics, with their stated priorities, dependencies and exit criteria.
Delivery ownership E01–E14 remain in scope; E07/E08 coordinate domain releases, E09–E14 own dedicated Knowledge implementation. Shared requirements are tracked once and referenced by dependent epics.
Priority clarification P0 offline typed/ink/hybrid authoring and KN-10 tools remain required; P1 extends advanced ink/PDF, downloaded collections and attachment controls. P1 knowledge proposals use bounded approval/audit; broader M02 actions remain P2.
Desktop offline Web stays online-first; assess full desktop offline editing as a separate future feasibility decision without weakening Android offline commitments or implying it is already delivered.

Integration decisions and risks

Decision / risk Disposition
Product authority SaveSphere is an independent product; module ownership follows its canonical domain contracts.
Stack Implement the selected SaveSphere stack with internal reusable components and shared domain services. Evaluate PowerSync only against documented self-hosting, privacy, conflict and recovery criteria; it is not a required second system.
iOS scope Keep iOS and HealthKit as conditional P2 expansion, with a separate feasibility gate.
Privacy conflict The action authorization policy and conservative raw-only constraints both apply; local PIN is not remote auth; no default raw upload.
Interaction-design validation Design SaveSphere interactions from its functional and accessibility requirements; validate consistency and owner-approved UX acceptance on supported devices.
Import fidelity Verify import fidelity, source hashes, privacy, backups and restoration. Local-only and raw-only data stays local unless the owner explicitly changes policy.
Verification limit Specification completeness does not establish implementation. Verify requirement-to-commit/test traceability, native device behavior and release evidence.

Link implementation issues, architecture decisions, tests and release evidence to stable requirement IDs. Internal reuse is appropriate when one implementation satisfies all linked contracts.

Home hosting, reliability and operations

Select a host environment from the deployment profile after validating automatic startup without interactive sign-in. Reserve CPU, RAM and storage for workstation use where the host is shared; run heavy indexing, OCR and AI jobs during permitted idle periods. Keep production and development databases, directories, secrets, ports and deployment profiles separate.

Required foundation Later / optional
API, Angular static web host, PostgreSQL, cloudflared Redis, if measurements justify caching or coordination
Durable .NET worker / scheduler, persistent file store Grafana dashboards, if built-in monitoring is insufficient
Encrypted backups, monitoring, restart policies Ollama/local inference, subject to hardware capacity
Health endpoints, logs, migrations, recovery documentation MQTT, Home Assistant, native sensor gateways
  • Automate boot/restart and service health checks; prevent host sleep during required availability. Plan for Windows updates, outages and disk failures. A UPS and independent backup device are recommended.
  • Use a 3-2-1 backup approach where practical: production plus independent local copy and encrypted off-site copy. Coordinate PostgreSQL and attachments, retain manifests and checksums, test restores on an isolated instance; do not keep the only backup on the host disk.
  • System screen shows CPU, RAM, storage, API/DB/tunnel/worker health, pending sync, job failures, backup age and restore history. Admin endpoints are restricted to explicitly trusted personal sessions. Avoid arbitrary remote shell or raw secrets in the UI.
  • Use versioned images, migration preflight, deployment scripts and rollback plans. Test reboot recovery and a restore on another machine; avoid promising high availability from one host.

Implementation and release checklist

  1. Approve the increment’s canonical requirement IDs, scope, target phase and feasibility conditions.
  2. Link each implemented behavior to its source commit, tests, measured results, date and owner acceptance.
  3. Verify permissions, Private Review, raw/local-only capture, lock behavior, provider gates and scope revocation on actual supported devices.
  4. Verify offline prayer, notifications, recovery, templates, follow-ups, nutrition review, live workouts and other workflows assigned to the increment.
  5. Account for import inputs, IDs, relationships, event history, privacy, original hashes, settings, rule versions, exports and restoration.
  6. Take independent encrypted backups and rehearse restore and rollback. Resolve critical defects, duplicate financial effects and unexplained data loss.
  7. Record conditional blockers and deferred scope honestly; do not label a partial capability fully delivered.

Capability coverage map

Coverage is at documented capability-family level. Each link leads to individually testable SaveSphere requirements. A mapped item remains planned until the corresponding implementation and test evidence are attached.
